s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute neurological deterioration with fever and focal neurological deficits
salient_findings: Hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on noncontrast head CT
T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule on brain MRI
key_facts: 19-year-old man with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use
Transferred for evaluation of altered mental status
Minimally responsive and febrile on arrival
Glasgow Coma Scale 10
Required intubation for airway protection
Left upper- and lower-limb weakness (strength 2/5 and 3/5)
No meningeal signs
Vital signs were stable
Leukocytosis (white blood cell count rising from 10.0 to 14.6 × 10^3/µL)
Urine toxicology positive for benzodiazepines and opiates
Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid
CSF with 538 WBCs/mm³ (57% polymorphonuclear leukocytes), protein 81 mg/dL, and glucose 57 mg/dL

shortlist.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: immunocompromised patient with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use, consistent with subacute neurological deterioration and focal neurological deficits

shortlist.label: CNS Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has hepatitis C, which increases the risk of TB, and presents with subacute neurological deterioration and fever

shortlist.label: Cerebral Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: immunocompromised patient with hepatitis C, consistent with subacute neurological deterioration and focal neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Brain Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: patient presents with fever, altered mental status, and focal neurological deficits, which are consistent with a brain abscess

shortlist.label: Neurosyphilis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has a history of intravenous heroin use, which increases the risk of syphilis, and presents with subacute neurological deterioration and focal neurological deficits

raw.rationale: The patient's immunocompromised state due to hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use, along with the presence of a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mass effect on imaging, and the progression of symptoms despite empirical antibiotic treatment, are consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy, particularly given the lack of enhancement after gadolinium and the negative CSF studies for other infectious causes.

rejected.label: CNS Tuberculosis
rejected.why: The lack of enhancement after gadolinium and the negative CSF studies for acid-fast bacilli make CNS Tuberculosis less likely.

rejected.label: Cerebral Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation and imaging findings, particularly the lack of enhancement after gadolinium, are not typical for Cerebral Toxoplasmosis.

rejected.label: Brain Abscess
rejected.why: The absence of ring enhancement on imaging and the negative CSF studies for bacterial causes make Brain Abscess less likely.

rejected.label: Neurosyphilis
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation and imaging findings, along with the lack of specific CSF findings suggestive of Neurosyphilis, make this diagnosis less likely.
